scope: ThinkSo local pull-request review and post-merge feedback trigger skills
rule: Do not require the trigger skills to launch their Python hosts from a detached origin/main checkout merely because a branch can edit the local scripts. For pull-request review, the accepted boundary is to inspect immutable author and head metadata first: owner-authored PRs proceed automatically, while any external author requires Mitchell's explicit approval bound to the exact head SHA before PR files or candidate code are fetched, and a new head invalidates approval. Post-merge feedback may invoke the local host directly while its JSON-only write validation and fresh-main retry remain intact.
rationale: PR #7 initially answered a valid candidate-trust concern with detached-main bootstrap ceremony. The owner rejected that operational model as mismatched to agent use and approved a narrower author/head authorization gate plus the existing guarded post-merge write path. Merge f22c7241d2884108d5321dde0f94d00ceea317c8 implements that project-specific boundary.
